column1: # The rules file of the ZAP baseline scan (.github/workflows/zap-baseline.yml, roadmap G7-03).
# It decides what a passive alert means to the build. Every alert ZAP raises is a WARN by default
# (informational ones included, in the mode ZAP's baseline runs in), and the workflow runs with
# `fail_action: true`, so a WARN or a FAIL that this file does not mention fails the job. The file
# started with NO exception: the first finding of a scan is a thing to read, and only a finding
# that is shown to be the intended behaviour of the product is added here. The ones below are what
# the first scan showed.
# Format: one rule per line, TAB-separated (a space is not a separator):
#   <rule id>  <IGNORE|INFO|WARN|FAIL>  (<rule name>)  <optional message, shown in the log>
# The first three fields are required: a line with fewer than two tabs makes ZAP stop with exit
# code 3 and no report, which the action reports as "failed to scan the target". The id and the
# name are in the scan's log and in its report (the artifact `zap-baseline-report-<attempt>`).
# A line starting with `#` is a comment, and so is nothing else.
# IGNORE removes the alert from the log's verdict. INFO keeps it in the log and in the run's
# summary and does not fail the job: use it for what is not a finding today but should stay in
# front of a reader, because its matches could change.
# What an IGNORE or an INFO owes, before it is merged:
#   1. A comment block above it saying WHY the behaviour is intended, in a sentence a reviewer who
#      has not seen the scan can check, with the section of docs/SECURITY.md (or the ADR) that
#      states it. "ZAP is wrong" is not a reason; "this cookie is read by the page's own script,
#      docs/SECURITY.md section 7" is.
#   2. The route it was seen on, when the rule is intended there and nowhere else. An IGNORE covers
#      every URL, and so does everything else on this page. The format scopes a rule to a route with
#      `<rule id>  OUTOFSCOPE  <url regex>`, which is what to prefer when only one route is the
#      exception; see the note below on when such a line is applied at all.
#   3. It never silences a finding to turn the job green. A real finding stays a WARN, the job stays
#      red, and the finding is written up where the maintainer reads it (a pull request, an issue,
#      docs/SECURITY.md section 12 "Accepted risks" if it is accepted).
# How the action reads this file, because it is not obvious and it is the reason the file can look
# inert: zaproxy/action-baseline hands the file to ZAP (`-c`) only when it holds at least one
# IGNORE line. A file of comments, or one that only moves a rule to FAIL or INFO or scopes it with
# OUTOFSCOPE, is never passed, and its lines are silently not applied. The day the first IGNORE is
# added the whole file starts to apply, every other line included. So after any edit, read the scan's
# log: an IGNORE, an INFO or an OUTOFSCOPE that did what it says shows as such in the summary.
# The exceptions. Each is something the first scan (ZAP 2.17.0, run 40398368412) showed and that
# is the intended behaviour of the product, or a plain false positive. In the mode ZAP's baseline
# runs in, an informational alert counts as a WARN too, so the four informational ones below have
# to be said once.
# Two findings of that scan are NOT here, on purpose, because they are not intended:
#   10055  CSP: style-src unsafe-inline   known and documented as a defect, docs/SECURITY.md
#                                         section 8 and the corrections table of section 14.7
#   90004  Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy   `crossOriginEmbedderPolicy: false` in
#                                         src/interface/http/middleware/securityHeaders.ts, with
#                                         no reason written anywhere
# They stay WARN, and the job stays red, until the product changes or the maintainer accepts the
# risk in docs/SECURITY.md section 12 and a line is added here that says so.
# 10010, Cookie No HttpOnly Flag. The only cookie an anonymous request is given is `es_csrf`, the
# double-submit CSRF value, which the page's own script has to read to send it back in the
# `X-CSRF-Token` header; on its own it is not a credential. docs/SECURITY.md "Cookie flags"
# (section 2) says `es_csrf` is not HttpOnly and section 7 says why, and csrf.test.ts asserts it
# ("Deliberately not HttpOnly").
# What this line costs. This scan never signs in or joins, so it cannot see the other cookies, and
# an IGNORE cannot be scoped to one cookie: it silences the rule for every cookie this scan
# reaches. Of those other cookies, the HttpOnly flag of `es_guest` (publicRoutes.test.ts), of
# `es_gallery` (galleryRoutes.test.ts) and of `es_device` (authRoutes.trustedDevice.test.ts) is
# asserted by a ring 4 test. That of `es_session`, the host's session, is asserted by none against
# the real server: authRoutes.test.ts asserts it on the cookie a logout clears, and nothing on the
# one a sign-in sets (server.ts, `httpOnly: true`). So with this line nothing guards it. It was
# found by the review of the pull request that added this scan, and is not fixed there.

column4: es_csrf is script-readable on purpose, docs/SECURITY.md sections 2 and 7

column1: # 10027, Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments. Informational. It greps comments for words
# such as BUG, DB, WHERE or TODO. What the first scan matched, read in its report, is prose: the
# comment Vite leaves in the shipped index.html about why the page stays French (a static file
# served to every request), the comment of favicon.svg, and a string inside the minified bundle.
# None held a credential, an address or an internal path. That is true of those matches only, and
# the report lists the first ten of them, so this is INFO and not IGNORE: a comment that starts to
# say more stays in front of a reader, and does not fail the job.

column4: prose comments of the shipped HTML and SVG at the first scan, read them

column1: # 10049, Storable but Non-Cacheable Content. Informational. index.html is `no-cache` on purpose: a
# guest who scans the QR code after a deploy must never be given a page that references assets which
# no longer exist (`mountClient`, src/interface/http/server.ts). Static files carry express's own
# `max-age=0`. Everything under /api is `no-store` by default (`noStoreByDefault`, same file).
# This id is the rule, not one alert: it also raises "Storable and Cacheable Content" and
# "Non-Storable Content", so a public route that regressed to a cacheable answer would be raised
# under it. That is why this is INFO and not IGNORE.

column4: index.html is no-cache by design, src/interface/http/server.ts

column1: # 10109, Modern Web Application. Informational, and a statement about the app rather than a finding:
# the web app is a single-page app (one index.html, scripts, no links), ZAP says so and advises its
# browser-driven spider. This scan gives its ordinary spider the pages instead, through the sitemap
# the workflow writes, for the reasons written beside `cmd_options` there.

column4: a single-page app by design, the workflow feeds the spider a sitemap

column1: # 10112, Session Management Response Identified. Informational: ZAP recognising `es_csrf` as a
# session token, a hint meant for its authenticated scans, which this one is not. Whether the
# cookie's flags are right is what 10010 above and docs/SECURITY.md section 7 are about.

column4: ZAP noticing es_csrf, a hint for authenticated scans
